qs.q: A 62-year-old diabetic patient presents with a chronic ulcer over the heel. On clinical examination, a sterile metal probe inserted into the wound base encounters a hard, gritty resistance that directly contacts the calcaneus. What is the best initial imaging modality to confirm the diagnosis of osteomyelitis?
o: Magnetic resonance imaging of the affected foot
Computed tomography angiography of the lower limb
Technetium bone scan with radionuclide labelling
Plain X-ray of the foot showing bone destruction
qs.e: MRI is the imaging test of choice for suspected osteomyelitis in diabetic foot ulcers, boasting a sensitivity and specificity of about 90%. Bone biopsy with culture remains the gold standard, but MRI is the preferred non-invasive imaging method.
qs.s: Diabetic Foot Ulcers: Neuropathy, Infection and Management: MCQs

qs.q: An 82-year-old woman recovering from a hip fracture presents with localized, non-blanchable erythema over her right calcaneus, with intact skin. What is the primary underlying pathophysiologic process responsible for this presentation?
o: Tissue tearing caused by tangential shear forces
Skin breakdown resulting from moisture maceration
Ischemia driven by sustained localized pressure
qs.e: Unrelieved external pressure exceeding microvascular capillary occlusion pressure directly causes tissue hypoxia and ischemia. Shear forces contribute to mechanical deformation but are secondary exacerbating factors to primary pressure-induced ischemia.
qs.s: Pressure Ulcers (Pressure Sores): Staging, Prevention and Treatment: MCQs
